skill.name: error-tracking-integrator
skill.description: Adds error tracking guidance for Sentry, Rollbar, and similar services, including setup, error boundaries, context, breadcrumbs, alerts, and source maps.
skill.summary: Integrates application error tracking and production debugging workflows.
skill.author: CrazyDubya

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline filenames, and process.env examples in documentation. The skill does provide legitimate error tracking guidance, but its context examples can transmit personal or business data to a third-party monitoring service if users do not minimize telemetry. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.suggestion: Show safer defaults that use stable internal identifiers, hash user identifiers when possible, and avoid sending email, usernames, order totals, or item counts unless required.
Add explicit instructions to keep DSNs and auth tokens in deployment secret stores, never commit them, and scope Sentry auth tokens to source map upload only.

remediation.issue: Broad Bash capability for package installation
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to request user confirmation before running package managers and to show the exact package names before installation.

semantic_findings.title: Potential Sensitive Telemetry Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The examples add user email, username, order totals, item counts, and order IDs to Sentry context. This is legitimate observability guidance, but it can send personal or business data to a third-party service if copied without minimization.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples explicitly attach user and order details to error events. The skill also includes scrubbing guidance, so the risk is contextual rather than clearly malicious.

content.value_statement: Production errors are hard to diagnose without context. This skill guides setup for monitoring, error boundaries, breadcrumbs, alerts, and privacy filtering.
actual_capabilities: Identifies common frontend and backend frameworks before choosing an error tracking approach.
Provides Sentry setup examples for React and Node.js with environment-based configuration.
Shows React error boundaries and manual exception capture patterns.
Adds user context, tags, custom context, and breadcrumbs to improve debugging.
Covers source maps, alerts, performance transactions, and basic sensitive data filtering.
limitations: It does not create provider accounts, projects, DSNs, or API tokens.
SDK names and integration APIs may need updates for current provider versions.
Telemetry fields must be reviewed for privacy, security, and compliance needs.
It does not replace tests, logging strategy, or incident response processes.

use_cases.title: Add Frontend Error Monitoring
use_cases.description: Install React error tracking, add an error boundary, and capture useful user actions before failures.

use_cases.title: Instrument Backend Exceptions
use_cases.description: Configure server-side monitoring for Express services with request handlers, error middleware, and environment labels.

use_cases.title: Improve Production Debugging
use_cases.description: Add source maps, alerts, tags, and release context so teams can triage production issues faster.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Basic Monitoring
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single app
prompt_templates.prompt: Add basic Sentry error tracking to this project. Detect the framework, list required packages, and configure the DSN through environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Add Error Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a React error boundary around the main application. Include a fallback UI and capture exceptions with useful tags.

prompt_templates.title: Add Context and Breadcrumbs
prompt_templates.prompt: Instrument this checkout flow with safe breadcrumbs, tags, and minimal user context. Avoid sending personal data unless necessary.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Production Observability
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure production error tracking with source maps, release tags, alert rules, sampling guidance, and a sensitive data review checklist.

output_examples.input: Add error tracking to my React app.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the React entry point, recommends the required monitoring package, adds initialization guidance, places an error boundary, and lists needed environment variables.

output_examples.input: Improve production debugging for an Express API.
output_examples.output: The response adds request and error middleware guidance, separates environments, suggests release tags, and defines alerts for new issues and error spikes.

output_examples.input: Review my Sentry context fields before launch.
output_examples.output: The response flags personal and business data, recommends safer identifiers, and gives a short checklist for filtering sensitive event payloads.

best_practices: Review every context field before sending it to an external monitoring service.
Keep provider tokens in secret stores and use separate projects for each environment.
Add release tags, source maps, and alert rules before production rollout.
anti_patterns: Do not send passwords, access tokens, payment data, or full request bodies in error events.
Do not hardcode DSNs or auth tokens in source code.
Do not enable high performance sampling without checking cost and data volume.

faq.question: Which error tracking services does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on Sentry examples and also references Rollbar, Bugsnag, Airbrake, and LogRocket as service options.

faq.question: Does it create my Sentry project?
faq.answer: No. You must create provider accounts, projects, DSNs, and tokens outside the skill workflow.

faq.question: Can it be used with frontend and backend apps?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for frontend frameworks and Node.js backend services.

faq.question: How does it handle sensitive data?
faq.answer: It includes basic scrubbing guidance, but you must review all telemetry fields before deployment.

faq.question: Does it support source maps?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes production source map guidance for readable stack traces.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
